title: Best Stand Mixers of 2026: 8 Top Picks for Every Baker
excerpt: The best stand mixers for every kind of baking, from the KitchenAid Artisan to the Bosch Universal Plus and Ankarsrum for bread, with a comparison table and buying guide.
html:
A good stand mixer takes the hard work out of baking: it creams butter and sugar, whips egg whites, and kneads bread dough while your hands are free. The right one depends on what you bake and how often, and the choice comes down to a few things: bowl size, motor power, tilt-head or bowl-lift design, and the attachments you might want later.

Quick answer: the KitchenAid Artisan 5-quart is the best stand mixer for most home bakers. For lots of bread, look at the Bosch Universal Plus or the heavy-duty Ankarsrum Original; for big batches, the KitchenAid Pro 600 bowl-lift; and for the best value, the Cuisinart SM-50.

The Best Stand Mixers of 2026: Quick Picks

Specifications come from the manufacturers’ listings; prices and stock change often, so confirm them on the product page.

Wattage isn’t the whole story: KitchenAid’s direct-drive motors are rated lower than some budget mixers but deliver steady power to the beater. Compare bowl size and design first.

How We Chose the Best Stand Mixers

1

Mixing performance

Planetary or bottom-drive action that reaches the whole bowl, from two egg whites to a double batch of cookie dough.

2

Dough handling

How well the mixer copes with stiff bread dough without straining or walking across the counter.

3

Capacity and size

Bowl capacity for the household, and height and weight for the space it will live in.

4

Included tools and attachments

Flat beater, dough hook and whisk in the box, and the range of optional attachments.

5

Brand, support and value

Established brands with parts and service available, at a fair price for what you get.

Detailed Reviews: The 8 Best Stand Mixers

1
Best Overall

KitchenAid Artisan Series 5-Quart Tilt-Head Stand Mixer (KSM150PS)

Best for: Most home bakers: cookies, cakes, frosting, whipped cream and the occasional loaf.

Check price on Amazon

The Artisan is the stand mixer most people picture, and for good reason. Its planetary mixing action moves the beater around the bowl as it spins, so batters and doughs come together without constant scraping, and the 5-quart stainless steel bowl holds about nine dozen cookies’ worth of dough or a double batch of cake batter.

It comes with a flat beater, a C-shaped dough hook, a 6-wire whip and a pouring shield, and the front power hub accepts more than ten KitchenAid attachments: pasta rollers, a meat grinder, a spiralizer and an ice cream bowl, among others. Ten speeds, a tilt-head that makes adding ingredients and changing beaters easy, and dozens of colors make it the default choice.

For very stiff bread dough made often, a bowl-lift or a Bosch or Ankarsrum is stronger; the Artisan handles a loaf or two at a time. In 2026 KitchenAid also launched the Artisan Plus, with a variable speed dial, 11 speed settings and a bowl light; the original Artisan remains the better-value buy.

Pros

  • Planetary mixing reaches the whole bowl
  • Flat beater, dough hook, 6-wire whip and pouring shield
  • Power hub for 10+ attachments
  • Dozens of colors
  • Tilt-head makes adding ingredients easy

Cons

  • Heavy (over 20 lb) to move
  • Not built for daily stiff bread dough
  • Tilt-head needs clearance above the counter

Verdict: The best stand mixer for most home kitchens.

2
Best Bowl-Lift

KitchenAid Pro 600 Series 6-Quart Bowl-Lift Stand Mixer (KP26M1X)

Best for: Bakers who make big batches, double recipes or bread every week.

Check price on Amazon

The Pro 600 trades the tilt-head for a bowl-lift: the head stays fixed and a lever raises the bowl to the beater. That rigid design, a 6-quart bowl and more power make it steadier with heavy bread dough and big batches.

It runs the same attachments as every KitchenAid with a power hub. Because the head doesn’t tilt, adding ingredients is easiest with the pouring shield, and it is tall, so measure the space under your cabinets.

Pros

  • 6-quart bowl for big batches
  • More powerful than tilt-head models
  • Stable with heavy dough
  • Same attachment hub

Cons

  • Tall: check under-cabinet space
  • Harder to add ingredients mid-mix
  • Heavier

Verdict: The KitchenAid to buy if you bake in large batches or knead bread often.

View the KitchenAid Pro 600 on Amazon

3
Best for Bread

Bosch Universal Plus Stand Mixer, 6.5 Quart, 500 Watt

Best for: Bread bakers who make several loaves at a time.

Check price on Amazon

The Bosch Universal Plus looks nothing like a KitchenAid: the motor sits under the bowl and drives the dough hook from below, and the bowl is open at the top so you can add flour while it runs. That design kneads large, stiff batches of bread dough without straining, which is why serious home bread bakers like it.

It is much lighter than a KitchenAid and has four speeds plus pulse. It is less elegant for small jobs like whipping a couple of egg whites, and its attachments are sold separately.

Pros

  • Kneads large batches of stiff dough
  • Add ingredients from above while it runs
  • Lightweight
  • 6.5-quart bowl

Cons

  • Not ideal for small quantities
  • Fewer speeds
  • Unusual look

Verdict: The best stand mixer for people who bake a lot of bread.

View the Bosch Universal Plus on Amazon

4
Best Heavy-Duty

Ankarsrum Original Stand Mixer (AKM6230), 7 Liter

Best for: Frequent bakers of sourdough, brioche and big batches.

Check price on Amazon

The Ankarsrum works differently from every other mixer here: the bowl turns while a dough roller and scraper knead against it, much like hand kneading. Reviewers single it out as the heavy-duty choice for frequent bread bakers, and its 7-liter bowl handles large batches.

It comes with a dough roller, dough knife, dough hook, a second plastic bowl with balloon and cookie whips, and a dust cover. It takes some learning, it costs more than most mixers here, and you should buy the 120-volt US version (the listing linked here).

Pros

  • Superb with bread and enriched doughs
  • 7-liter bowl
  • Many tools included
  • Built to last

Cons

  • Learning curve
  • Premium price
  • Check voltage on the listing

Verdict: The heavy-duty pick for bakers who knead dough every week.

View the Ankarsrum Original on Amazon

5
Best Value

Cuisinart SM-50 Precision Master 5.5-Quart Stand Mixer

Best for: Anyone who wants a full-size stand mixer for less than a KitchenAid.

Check price on Amazon

The Cuisinart SM-50 gives you a slightly bigger bowl than the Artisan (5.5 quarts), 12 speeds and a 500-watt motor, usually for noticeably less. It comes with a flat mixing paddle, dough hook, whisk and a splash guard with a pour spout.

It handles everyday baking well. KitchenAid’s attachment range is bigger and its resale value higher, but if you just want to mix and knead, the Cuisinart is excellent value.

Pros

  • 5.5-quart bowl
  • 12 speeds
  • Splash guard with pour spout
  • Strong value

Cons

  • Fewer attachments than KitchenAid
  • Fewer color options

Verdict: The best value full-size stand mixer.

View the Cuisinart SM-50 on Amazon

6
Best Budget KitchenAid

KitchenAid Classic Series 4.5-Quart Tilt-Head Stand Mixer (K45SS)

Best for: Small households that want a KitchenAid at the lowest price.

Check price on Amazon

The Classic is KitchenAid’s simplest stand mixer. Compared with the Artisan it has a smaller 4.5-quart bowl, a little less power and no pouring shield, but it uses the same planetary mixing and the same power hub, so every attachment fits.

For cookies, cakes and frosting for a small household it is all you need. Big batches and frequent bread dough are better in a larger model.

Pros

  • Lowest-priced KitchenAid
  • Same attachment hub
  • Planetary mixing
  • Compact

Cons

  • 4.5-quart bowl
  • Less power than the Artisan
  • Fewer colors

Verdict: The most affordable way into a KitchenAid.

View the KitchenAid Classic on Amazon

7
Best Budget

Hamilton Beach 4-Quart Electric Stand Mixer, 7 Speeds

Best for: Occasional bakers and first-time buyers on a tight budget.

Check price on Amazon

The Hamilton Beach covers occasional baking for a fraction of the price of the big names: a 4-quart stainless bowl, 7 speeds, planetary mixing, and a flat beater, dough hook and whisk.

It is light and easy to store, but it isn’t made for heavy bread dough or daily use; choose a larger model if you bake often.

Pros

  • Very affordable
  • Light and easy to store
  • Planetary mixing
  • Three attachments included

Cons

  • Not for heavy dough
  • Smaller bowl
  • Lighter build

Verdict: The budget pick for occasional baking.

View the Hamilton Beach 4 qt on Amazon

8
Best Large Budget

Aucma 6.5-Quart 660-Watt Stand Mixer

Best for: Bakers who want a big bowl without spending much.

Check price on Amazon

The Aucma pairs a large 6.5-quart bowl with a 660-watt motor at a budget price. It comes with a whisk, dough hook, mixing beater and a splash guard with an opening for adding ingredients.

Aucma lists it at 76 decibels and a 4.4-pound maximum mix. Build quality and long-term durability are not on the level of KitchenAid or Bosch, so treat it as a budget big-bowl option.

Pros

  • Large 6.5-quart bowl
  • 660-watt motor
  • Splash guard included
  • Budget price

Cons

  • Lighter build
  • Noisier than premium models
  • Fewer attachments

Verdict: A big bowl on a small budget.

Stand Mixer Buying Guide

The essentials below are covered step by step in our how to choose a stand mixer guide for first-time buyers.

Tilt-head, bowl-lift or bottom drive

DesignHow it worksBest for
Tilt-headThe head tilts back to change beaters and add ingredientsMost home baking; easy to use
Bowl-liftThe head stays fixed and a lever lifts the bowlBig batches and heavy dough
Bottom drive (Bosch)The motor turns the tool from below; the bowl is open on topLarge bread batches
Rotating bowl (Ankarsrum)The bowl turns against a roller and scraperFrequent bread and enriched doughs

Bowl size

BowlGood for
4 to 4.5 qtOne or two people, occasional baking
5 to 5.5 qtMost households: a double batch of cookies, a loaf of bread
6 qt and upBig batches, several loaves, frequent baking

Attachments

Every mixer here comes with the three basic tools: a flat beater (paddle) for batters and cookie dough, a dough hook for kneading, and a wire whip for cream and egg whites. KitchenAid’s power hub adds optional attachments such as a pasta roller, meat grinder, spiralizer and ice cream bowl.

Height, weight and noise

Measure the space under your cabinets, leaving room for a tilt-head to open. Heavier mixers stay put on the counter with stiff dough; lighter ones are easier to store.

Which Stand Mixer for Your Baking?

For most home bakers

Start with the KitchenAid Artisan.

Cookies, cakes, frosting and the occasional loaf, with room to grow into attachments.

For bread every week

Choose the Bosch Universal Plus or the Ankarsrum Original.

Both are built for stiff, large doughs. See also our best stand mixer for bread dough.

For cakes and frosting

The KitchenAid Artisan or the Cuisinart SM-50.

Smooth, even mixing for batters and buttercream; more in stand mixer for cakes.

For big batches

Look at the KitchenAid Pro 600.

A 6-quart bowl-lift for double recipes and holiday baking.

On a budget

Get the Hamilton Beach 4 qt or the KitchenAid Classic.

Affordable mixers for occasional baking.

Is a Stand Mixer Worth It?

If you bake at least a few times a month, or make bread, a stand mixer is worth it: it saves time, mixes more evenly and frees your hands. If you only whip cream or mix the odd batter, a hand mixer may be enough; our stand mixer vs hand mixer guide compares the two, and what is a stand mixer covers the advantages and disadvantages.

Stand Mixer Care Tips

  • Start on the lowest speed when adding dry ingredients, then increase gradually.
  • Don’t overload the bowl with stiff dough; knead large batches in two.
  • On KitchenAid tilt-head mixers, check the beater-to-bowl clearance with the dime test and adjust the screw if the beater scrapes or misses the bottom.
  • Wash the bowl and tools after each use (check which are dishwasher safe), and wipe the body with a damp cloth.

Stand Mixer FAQ

What is the best stand mixer?

For most home bakers, the KitchenAid Artisan 5-quart. For frequent bread baking, the Bosch Universal Plus or the Ankarsrum Original; for the best value, the Cuisinart SM-50.

Is KitchenAid better than Cuisinart?

KitchenAid has the bigger attachment range, more colors and stronger resale value; Cuisinart often gives a larger bowl and more speeds for less. Both make dependable everyday mixers.

What size stand mixer do I need?

A 5 to 5.5-quart bowl suits most households. Choose 6 quarts or more for big batches and frequent bread, and 4 to 4.5 quarts for one or two people.

How many watts should a stand mixer have?

Most good tilt-head mixers are 250 to 500 watts, and bowl-lift and heavy-duty models more. Wattage isn’t everything: design and gearing matter as much as the number.

Can a stand mixer knead bread dough?

Yes, with the dough hook. For frequent or large batches, a bowl-lift, the Bosch Universal Plus or the Ankarsrum handles stiff dough better than a small tilt-head.

Tilt-head or bowl-lift?

Tilt-head is easier for everyday baking and fits under more cabinets. Bowl-lift is sturdier for heavy dough and big batches.

What is the new KitchenAid Artisan Plus?

Launched in 2026, it is an updated 5-quart tilt-head with a variable speed dial, 11 speed settings and a bowl light. The original Artisan remains the better value for most people.

Final Verdict

  • Best Overall KitchenAid Artisan: The best stand mixer for most home kitchens.
  • Best Bowl-Lift KitchenAid Pro 600: The KitchenAid to buy if you bake in large batches or knead bread often.
  • Best for Bread Bosch Universal Plus: The best stand mixer for people who bake a lot of bread.
  • Best Heavy-Duty Ankarsrum Original: The heavy-duty pick for bakers who knead dough every week.
  • Best Value Cuisinart SM-50: The best value full-size stand mixer.
  • Best Budget KitchenAid KitchenAid Classic: The most affordable way into a KitchenAid.
Our Top Recommendation

KitchenAid Artisan Series 5-Quart Tilt-Head Stand Mixer (KSM150PS)

For most kitchens we recommend the KitchenAid Artisan 5-quart: it mixes evenly, handles everyday baking with ease and grows with you through attachments.

Bake bread every week? Choose the Bosch Universal Plus. Want the best value? The Cuisinart SM-50.
